context.body: A remembered saying from Acts 1 is applied to a new event involving Gentiles.

context.body: The event in apostolic proclamation · Acts 11:15–18

observations.body: Peter explains the Spirit’s coming on Gentiles by remembering the Lord’s contrast between John’s water baptism and baptism in the Holy Spirit.
observations.label: Peter remembers Jesus’ words about John and the Spirit: action

observations.body: The Jerusalem hearers become quiet, glorify God, and recognize life-giving repentance among Gentiles.
observations.label: Peter remembers Jesus’ words about John and the Spirit: response

observations.body: Spirit fell on them · remembered the Lord’s word · John baptized with water · same gift
observations.label: Words in Acts 11:15–18

payload.posture: Read Acts 11:15–18 as the event in apostolic proclamation evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Peter treats the remembered contrast as evidence, but the passage does not erase every difference between Pentecost and Caesarea.
payload.title: Peter remembers Jesus’ words about John and the Spirit
